summary: Jinah Kim specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 2001–2007) under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held posts at Vanderbilt University, the Institute for Advanced Study, and Harvard University.

Jinbo Shi is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology who studied at Minzu University of China (circa 1958–1962). He held appointments at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, including its Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology.
Jinchuan Wan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Wan has served as a professor at Fo Guang University (circa 2000) and National Central University.
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. Yin served as Director at the University of Hong Kong from circa 2005 to 2014.

Jing-shen Tao is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University, later serving as a fellow at Academia Sinica (circa 1969–1976) and Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (circa 1976–2003).
Jingkong (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Thomé H. Fang in 1949 and Bingnan Li from circa 1958 to 1968.

Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki, Chen held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of British Columbia.

Jinhua Jia specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll and held posts at City University of Hong Kong and the Institute for Advanced Study.
Jinling He works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University circa 2005–2008 under the supervision of Koki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University from circa 2006 to 2009 under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.

Jinshi Fan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (circa 1958–1963). She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (circa 1998–2014) and held a post at Lanzhou University.

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (circa 1957–1988) and as professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (circa 1996–2004).

Jiro Watanabe (1931–2008) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1950–1957). He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1965–1992), Seijo University, and the Open University of Japan (circa 1992–2002).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from circa 1952 to 1959.

Jitendranath Mohanty (1928–2023) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Göttingen. He held faculty posts at the University of Calcutta, the University of Oklahoma, and Temple University.
Jitsuaki Oshika is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and later served as a professor at Toyo University.

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (circa 1934–1941) and served as director of the Institute of World Religions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (circa 1964–1985).

Joachim Gentz specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen (circa 2002–2006) before becoming Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh in circa 2006.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna in 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (circa 1924–1935) and as Professor at the University of Chicago in 1950.
